transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47 mins | Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Dana Holt (Head of ML, Pioneer Robotics), Rajiv Patel (Platform Eng), Selma Ortiz (CTO)

[00:00] Olivia Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm olivia chen, i'm the account lead for redwood inference. marco is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Selma Ortiz: doing well, thanks. little tight schedule today.
[00:10] Dana Holt: yeah thanks. excited to dig in - main item for us is validating cost model for a POC before committing to dedicated capacity.
[00:17] Olivia Chen: perfect. agenda - confirm success criteria, get workload sizing, align on benchmarks and timeline, then share a draft unit economics model with batching/caching knobs. sound good?
[00:26] Rajiv Patel: yep that works.
[00:28] Marco Diaz: i'll lead the technical parts - quick disclaimer, transcript may have some auto-typos.
[00:33] Olivia Chen: first, success criteria - selma, dana, can you share what success looks like for the POC?
[00:39] Dana Holt: sure. two things: 1) performance - latency under 400ms tail for user-facing calls at our target concurrency, and 2) unit cost - we need to model staying under $25k/month for a 2M-user pilot. if either of those blow up, the execs will require answers.
[00:56] Selma Ortiz: and security - must be able to run in our VPC with KMS integration and SOC 2 level logs.
[01:03] Olivia Chen: totally. that's aligned with Redwood Private/Dedicated options.
[01:07] Marco Diaz: quick question on traffic profile - dana, what are avg tokens per request and peak qps?
[01:12] Dana Holt: average prompt 80 tokens, average completion 220 tokens - so ~300 tokens per call. Peak is currently 120 rps per region but for POC we expect to simulate ~30-40 rps sustained per pool.
[01:24] Rajiv Patel: also variability: 40% of calls are short (<= 128 tokens), 45% mid (129-512), 15% long (>512).
[01:31] Marco Diaz: that's useful. okay rough calc: 300 tokens/call * 40 rps sustained = 12,000 tokens/sec = ~1.04B tokens/day if it ran 24/7 but for the pilot you'll be lower - do you have expected monthly tokens for the POC?
[01:44] Dana Holt: for the pilot we budgeted ~600M tokens/month initially.
[01:48] Olivia Chen: great - that'll drive the cost modeling.
[01:50] Marco Diaz: i'll walk through two approaches - hosted API and dedicated pool. hosted gives fastest time-to-value, dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost for sustained heavy workloads.
[02:00] Marco Diaz: baseline hosted per-token unit: for example model M-7B we typically quote ~$0.00035 per input token + $0.0007 per output token - approximate blended hosted cost ~ $0.0006/token. that's a rough public-facing example, your negotiated price will vary.
[02:17] Dana Holt: ok, so at 600M tokens/month at $0.0006 that's $360k - that's way higher than our $25k.
[02:25] Selma Ortiz: yeah that number is alarming, what's the levers?
[02:29] Marco Diaz: right - batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, and routing to cheaper model variants for low-latency portions are the main levers. also dedicated pools reduce unit GPU costs.
[02:39] Olivia Chen: to be clear, those hosted list prices are comparable to other vendors; dedicated can bring per-token down significantly depending on batching and utilization.
[02:47] Marco Diaz: example dedicated math: assume a dedicated GPU node runs 24/7 and with batching + CPU/GPU kernels optimized we can get effective cost to, say, $0.00008-$0.00012 per token for a mid/large model depending on sequence length and batch efficiency. if you hit 600M tokens at $0.00010 that's $60k/mo - still above $25k but much closer.
[03:08] Rajiv Patel: those are big gaps. what drives the difference between $0.0006 and $0.0001? is it mostly batching?
[03:14] Marco Diaz: batching and prefix/KV cache. if many calls share common prefixes - e.g., same system prompt or template - you can cache KV states and only compute deltas. that can reduce compute by up to 40-60% for certain flows. Also sequence length matters - quantized kernels (q4_0 / int8) reduce memory and can improve throughput which lowers cost.
[03:32] Dana Holt: for us, system prompt is large but very consistent - looks promising for caching. also many requests are short.
[03:38] Marco Diaz: great; using your distribution (40% short) the effective token cost after caching might drop to $0.00006-$0.00009 on dedicated. with 600M tokens that's $36k-$54k. if you can reduce monthly token volume for the pilot to ~250-300M, you might hit the $25k target with aggressive caching and smaller model variants.
[03:55] Olivia Chen: one practical path: POC runway where we run a 2-week benchmark at realistic loads to measure effective tokens consumed, caching hit rate, and tail latency. we will produce a unit economics sheet with knobs toggled: batch size (min/max), KV cache TTL & hit rate, quantization profile, and model variant routing.
[04:11] Selma Ortiz: timeline - how quickly can we run that benchmark? we want results before year-end.
[04:15] Marco Diaz: we can spin up a small dedicated pool for a 24-72 hour soak within 48 hours of access details. for a realistic run we'd want at least 72h to see autoscale behavior and cache warm-up.
[04:25] Rajiv Patel: access details - we'll need VPC peering and a service account with restricted KMS access. can you support SAML/SSO for console access?
[04:33] Olivia Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO and can integrate with your IdP; for the POC we can do access via a temporary service account and then switch to SAML before production. KMS integration supported for Redwood Private / Dedicated.
[04:44] Dana Holt: what about logs and audit trail? execs need immutable audit logs for any production call.
[04:49] Marco Diaz: we provide request-level audit logs, token counts, and model versioning in the console. we also ship a syslog/S3 sink for retention. that meets SOC 2 requirements typically - we'll share our security pack.
[04:59] Olivia Chen: action item: i'll send the security docs and SOC 2 summary with the pricing spreadsheet.
[05:04] Selma Ortiz: good.
[05:05] Marco Diaz: back to cost math - i'll show a quick worked example in the notes. take your 300 tokens/call average: at 40 rps sustained, that's 12k tokens/sec or ~1.0B tokens/day if 24/7. but pilots rarely run 24/7 - your 600M/mo is realistic for a limited pilot.
[05:20] Marco Diaz: scenario A (hosted): blended $0.0006/token -> 600M * 0.0006 = $360k/mo. scenario B (dedicated, conservative): $0.00012/token -> 600M * 0.00012 = $72k/mo. scenario C (dedicated + caching/quant): $0.00006/token -> 600M * 0.00006 = $36k/mo.
[05:39] Dana Holt: still over $25k. could we use model routing - smaller model for short calls and larger for long?
[05:44] Marco Diaz: yep - hybrid routing is effective. if 60% of calls can be served by a smaller, cheaper model (e.g., a 2-4B variant) and only 40% need the 7B+, you can reduce blended cost a lot. example blended after routing: 0.00003/token for small model, 0.00012 for large. blended might be ~0.00007-0.00008/token -> 600M * 0.00008 = $48k/mo.
[06:03] Rajiv Patel: can you push any promotions or committed utilization discounts for a POC?
[06:07] Olivia Chen: we typically offer a POC pricing package: discounted dedicated hourly rates for the duration of the POC and a credit against first committed month. we'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[06:16] Selma Ortiz: fine. what about latency targets - you mentioned 400ms tail. is that achievable with batching? batching can improve throughput but hurts tail latency.
[06:25] Marco Diaz: correct tradeoff. continuous batching in our runtime allows small batch windows to reduce latency impact; for example a 10-20ms batch window can give higher throughput with modest tail latency change. for a 300-token average with optimized kernels, we can meet sub-400ms tail in many cases, but long sequences will exceed that. that's why we also use model routing: short/medium sequences served with low-latency model variants.
[06:47] Dana Holt: ok so POC must capture tail latency percentiles and cost per effective token with knobs: batching window, batch size max, kv cache TTL/hit rate, and quantization profile.
[06:58] Marco Diaz: exactly. we'll run controlled benchmarks to sweep those knobs and produce a surface of cost vs latency.
[07:05] Olivia Chen: we'll also include a section for failure modes: what happens when capacity is constrained - our smart routing can fall back to hosted variants to avoid outages, but that affects cost.
[07:15] Rajiv Patel: can you simulate that in the benchmark? like force a capacity limit and see fallback behavior?
[07:19] Marco Diaz: yes, we can simulate constrained capacity and measure latency and cost when fallback triggers. we'll document the policy used.
[07:26] Dana Holt: about metrics - what will you instrument and share?
[07:29] Marco Diaz: we'll capture request-level: input tokens, output tokens, latency p50/p95/p99, batch sizes, cache hit/miss counts, GPU utilization, and throughput. compiled into the Redwood Console dashboard and a csv export.
[07:41] Selma Ortiz: excellent. is there a way to estimate cost per active user or per session? that's what finance wants.
[07:46] Olivia Chen: yes - if you give us expected sessions/day and average tokens/session we can compute cost per active user. can you share those?
[07:52] Dana Holt: we estimate 0.25 sessions per user per day for pilot, target user base 2M but active users for pilot maybe 50k. avg session ~4 calls.
[08:00] Marco Diaz: quick calc: 50k users * 4 calls * 300 tokens ~ 60M tokens per day? wait that's too high. Sorry let me recalc: 50k * 4 calls = 200k calls/day * 300 tokens = 60M tokens/day -> ~1.8B tokens/month. that's larger than your earlier 600M.
[08:18] Dana Holt: ah yes our earlier 600M was too low if all those users are active. the 600M assumed smaller active user set. we need to reconcile numbers.
[08:25] Selma Ortiz: we'll get the definitive expected sessions and active users - dana will follow up.
[08:29] Dana Holt: yes i'll send a corrected traffic matrix.
[08:32] Marco Diaz: good. that will materially change the unit economics.
[08:35] Olivia Chen: aside from cost numbers, are there any must-have technical constraints?
[08:39] Rajiv Patel: data residency - all POC data must remain in our AWS account and not be used for model training.
[08:45] Marco Diaz: understood - for dedicated/private deployments we support data isolation and do not use customer request data for model training; we'll put that in the legal/security docs.
[08:54] Selma Ortiz: any concerns about model drift or quality regressions - we need to baseline accuracy metrics.
[08:59] Marco Diaz: we can run your eval prompt set and measure perplexity/ROUGE/whatever metrics you use. Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts if quality drops between model versions.
[09:09] Dana Holt: timeline: we need a 2-3 week POC that includes a 72h benchmark and then 1 week to analyze results. can you commit to delivering analysis within 7 business days after the run?
[09:20] Marco Diaz: yes - typical turnaround is 3-5 business days for the report. we'll aim for 5 to be conservative.
[09:26] Olivia Chen: so proposed schedule: 12/17 Olivia sends docs & pricing. 12/20 customer shares sample workload. 12/22 SE provisions test pool. 12/23-12/26 run 72h benchmark (holiday window noted). 12/29 analysis review meeting.
[09:41] Selma Ortiz: that timeline works if we can get access early.
[09:44] Rajiv Patel: question on telemetry: can we get raw token logs? we need raw per-call token counts for cost reconciliation.
[09:50] Marco Diaz: yes, we can provide raw logs (anonymized if needed) and aggregated dashboards.
[09:54] Dana Holt: pricing ask: if the POC shows we can get to $0.00005/token with caching + routing, do you offer a commitment discount to get to our $25k target?
[10:03] Olivia Chen: we can discuss commitment tiers - for sustained committed capacity we can negotiate below $0.00005/token in some cases depending on model and utilization. i'll flag pricing for the commercial team to include in the POC offer.
[10:15] Marco Diaz: last technical note - quantization quality: for some of your LLM tasks we typically see small quality delta moving from fp16 to q4_0 but q2/q3 may degrade more; so part of the benchmark will include quality regression checks.
[10:28] Dana Holt: good, include those evals in the plan.
[10:31] Olivia Chen: recap of next steps: send benchmark & pricing + security pack; customer to send traffic matrix & sample corpus; SE to provision and run 72h benchmark; follow-up meeting 12/29 to review results.
[10:43] Selma Ortiz: perfect.
[10:44] Rajiv Patel: one more - who is the point for billing and contracting questions?
[10:48] Olivia Chen: that's me; i'll loop in our commercial rep on the follow-up.
[10:52] Dana Holt: thanks everyone, we'll get the traffic matrix by end of week.
[10:56] Olivia Chen: thanks - i'll send the plan later today.
[10:59] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has minor auto-transcription errors (names/terms). Shared artifacts referenced: pricing_spreadsheet.xlsx, benchmark_plan.md, redwood_security_pack.pdf.

Benchmarks & knobs discussed (summary):
- Workload sizing: customer-provided distribution: short 40%, mid 45%, long 15%; avg ~300 tokens/call; pilot target initially quoted 600M tokens/mo but to be revalidated.
- Cost levers: batching window (10-50ms), max batch size, KV/prefix caching (expected 30-60% savings if warm), quantization profile (q4_0/int8 preferred), model routing (small model for short calls).
- Example cost scenarios calculated during call: hosted blended ~ $0.0006/token; dedicated conservative ~ $0.00012/token; dedicated + caching ~ $0.00006/token -> 600M = $36k/mo.
- Success criteria for POC: tail latency < 400ms for user-facing short calls, unit economic target (customer target $25k/mo), security controls (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and quality baselines passed for eval set.

References to follow-up artifacts:
- pricing_spreadsheet.xlsx (Redwood commercial team)
- benchmark_plan.md (Marco Diaz)
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and cost modeling. Primary constraints: target latency <400ms, budget target ~$25k/mo for pilot. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, caching, batching, quantization, model routing. Action items: Redwood to send pricing and security docs; customer to share traffic matrix; SE to run 72h benchmark; follow-up 2026-12-29.
